bug: Typing ls in a manual terminal could display l[REDACTED] and trigger cursor/history replay.
cause: Terminal redaction replaced any trailing credential prefix, including a single ordinary character. Tests reproduced the failure with the synthetic browser token, model key and SSH password.
fix: Sanitize accumulated output and screen snapshots with complete credential matching. Do not replace an ordinary suffix just because it is the beginning of a credential. Raw snapshots retained in memory still allow complete credentials received across PTY reads to be redacted.
regression: New regression tests failed on the original implementation, then passed after the fix.
Ordinary ls, pwd, processes, Chinese text and ANSI-colored prompts remain unchanged.
Complete model, SSH and browser credentials remain redacted.
Credential split across three received chunks is redacted in persisted output and live screen observations.
Real local bash PTY preserves l -> ls -> backspace -> ls, with no false redaction marker.
Existing raw-input ownership, split-UTF8 and title-redaction tests passed.

tests.browser: Isolated temporary home and loopback fixture. Typed l then s, backspaced and typed s again. Actual terminal displayed ls correctly. No commands executed, no model calls or remote SSH requests. Fixture and test tab closed.

desktop.runtime: Relaunched installed Lake Dev and verified DEV marker, idle chat and preserved model selection. Release app/data untouched.
